entry.title: Reading Log #6
entry.content:
Here is what I read from 7th to 17th September 2026.

Blogs

  • Maybe We Shouldn’t Be Reviewing All This Code

    I have been thinking about the same problem in the background for a while now, i.e. AI agents are dumping a huge amount of code and how do humans catch up?

  • Invisible Companies

    Must read if you are interested in “Business”.

  • Exit the Cave

    Ain’t it fun, living in the real world?

  • How to protect yourself from workslop

  • Can We Stop With the Uptime Percentages?

    I always translate uptime percent to be “how much time this was down for the past 30 days?” — it takes a while. The author suggests to directly give that information instead of the cryptic percentage (for general audience).

  • The irrational effectiveness of the Pi harness

    Pi again!

  • Every Customer Gets the Same Software. That’s Ending.

    Interesting point to think about in the current timeline.

  • There are many agent harnesses, but this one is mine.

  • The oldest architecture in computing

    Nice! Didn’t expect what the answer was.

  • Advice to Young Developers

    Got me thinking — what advice do I have?

  • The Safest Job from AI may be Writing

    I am convinced!

  • Rich, fully attributed context timeout errors in Go

    Good to read a “Go” post after a long while.

  • Writing About Writing

    Inspiring! It actually gave me an idea that might allow myself to write more.

  • You have to beat the models at something

    Wow, this is the second post that this week that relays that “writing” is one of the things that is more human in the age of AI.

  • ⭐ A Billion Dollars

    The first ever essay that I got to share with my sister!

  • You need to find product-market fit again (sorry)

  • A Calendar View For My Blog

  • Joy & Curiosity #98

    I read this one regularly but missed adding it in some of my previous reading logs.

  • Unsung at 500: behind the scenes

Books

  • ⭐ ✅ Keep Going

    (read 200 pages)

    Fantastic book! Must-read for people who are interested in doing art.

  • ⭐ How Will You Measure Your Life?

    (read 82 pages)

    Definitely altering who I am!

  • Make It Stick

    (read 41 pages)

  • Fahrenheit 451

    (read 7 pages)

  • Introduction to Information Retrieval

    (read 6 pages)

  • Tools of Titans

    (read 4 pages, plus a few more at random)

entry.title: Reading Log #5
entry.content:
I have been travelling the past 2 weeks and mostly spent time with a book during my reading time.

Here is what I read from 24th August to 6th September 2026.

Blogs

  • The end of programming

    AI models have gotten so good that it is becoming trivial to produce a lot of code in a day. Almost unreasonable amount of code that it would take even days to read through and get into them. I have been facing similar situation recently. Dealing with them is going to get normal. Let us figure out how to navigate this!

  • Why I am shutting down my bookstore in New Delhi

    I have become interested in bookstores recently. Tried visiting some new ones. Trying to get a sense for how it would feel to run a bookstore. The one that was closed in the blog post was a 30 years old bookstore. If something that had been running for such a long time could come to close, why?

  • Small Models Have Arrived

  • What is a Harness?

    Good intro!

  • Rebuilding Linear’s delta sync read path

    Interesting. This has made a few more interesting questions to delve on. Going to explore a bit. What are inverted indexes? What is the purpose of GIN?

  • Revised Rules of Engineering Leadership

  • Huzzah

    Same sentiment as post that I shared at the top. Huge amounts of code are getting written with AI these days. It is getting out of hand. I suspect that there is place for tools like this that help humans to have their understanding in sync with what AI produces. I am looking forward to more new ideas and tools like this. It is upto us to figure this out now!

  • AI-pilling our company: lessons learned

    Good takeaways. This is how most software teams will look like — they will face all the points mentioned in this post and have some version of the agent powering the team.

  • The Bottlenecks for AI-Driven System Design: why principal engineers are not (yet) obsolete

    What is a hill-climbing exercise? I notice this term being used when discussing about performance.

Books

  • Essentialism

    (read 203 pages)

    Finished this book. It gave me a sense of calm and the courage to ask “what is essential here?” whenever I like to.

  • Zen Pencils

    (read 9 pages)

    Make gifts for people - John Green

    Advice for Beginners - Ira Glass

  • Make it Stick

    (read 5 pages)

  • Fahrenheit 451

    (read 32 pages)

    This is going to be the first fiction for me this year. I want to get more into fictional works and enjoy them as much as I enjoy non-fictions. Planning to alternate fiction and non-fiction - let us see how it goes!

entry.title: Reading Log #4
entry.content:
Here is what I read from 17th to 23rd August 2026.

Blogs

  • Build something to disagree with

    Loved it!

  • Build Wide, Ship Narrow

    I have been personally having trouble in asking AI to come up with a design doc because it usually dumps a whole lot of 8 to 12 pages for a simple feature work. I arrived at a point that this post suggests to do first after experimentation: first thing to do is make AI ask you a lot of questions. The blog author tells about a skill for it: grill-me (tried it, pretty awesome!).

  • Thirty Percent Feedback

    If you are working at / building a startup, this might be a good read. My guess is that building a culture like this is probably what we might want for a startup and people in those startups to succeed. I don’t know if I am making sense, but I like blog posts like this which give a new or contrarian mental model that I might want to consider. TIL YC makes startups demo every week. The post is from 2014, so not sure if this is true anymore.

  • The Personal Reset

    Nice to associate a term for this. I personally am into a personal reset, 3 weeks in. My main personal reset component is to read blogs/books before sleep. More strictly until I find myself in a sleepy state.

  • Reflecting on My Failure to Build a Billion-Dollar Company

  • Devtools must be open source

    Made sense before AI and makes sense even more with AI.

  • drop that meet link

    Reminded me of the times I used to work in offices and the random chats that occur with colleagues in the physical space. I do miss those chats in remote setup sometimes.

  • AI;DR (AI; Didn’t Read)

    I am going to use this acronym both with humans and AI to let it rewrite the response in a manner that will help in unslopping. But yeah, never send slop to friends. Always handcraft.

  • How things win

    Post from the creator of Obsidian (one of my favorite pieces of software).

  • The Antithesis Principle

    I couldn’t fully internalize it.

  • the task isn’t the job

  • This too shall pass

  • 24 things I believe

    Loved all the points. My favorite is point (1). I was thinking of getting into music. Point (10) was a surprise and I consider it my signboard to pick up some music lessons.

  • When to join a startup

    Identify the risks and understand what you are dealing with.

  • How to Choose a Startup

    If you are working in startups or planning to go work for one, then this might be the good read for you.

Books

  • Essentialism

    (read 29 pages)

entry.title: Reading Log #3
entry.content:
Here is what I read from 8th to 16th August 2026.

Blogs

  • Reflections on my relationship with social media

    My usage of social media is already low. I can go on days without opening Instagram. My Twitter/X usage has been spiking up a bit these days, so I looked around to see if there is something out there to help me. It is a solid post and I read it to gain more momentum to be more productive with how I use my time. There was this one point about “environments” that resonated with me.

  • If AI Writes All the Code, What Do the Programmers Do?

    I liked the “Do I Enjoy This?” section. One particular quote:

    My job isn’t to write code, my job is to fix problems and to ship new features, and “write code” was just the way I got that done before.

  • You don’t have to be smart if you can think clearly

    The difference between a “smart” engineer and a “strong” engineer is how they react to problems that aren’t solved instantly.

  • What is a product?

    A short essay about what is a product.

    If nobody uses it or cares, is it still a product? What makes a product is its usage. If nobody is using the thing you built, you don’t have a product, you have a toy. Have fun playing with it.

  • River binaries will get 10 kB lighter

    Good to read something Go related after a long time.

  • Joining Cursor

    I have been following Fatih’s journey for a while. I don’t think he will discover this blog, but if he did somehow: “congrats, buddy! I am watching this space closely and I look forward to your updates.”

  • Touring The Consensus, six months in

    I lurk around on the Software Internals discord and know about the Consensus project that Phil Eaton was working on. I haven’t had a chance to check it closely myself and this post came up as a good reminder of what the project has evolved into. I am exploring the site as I write this.

  • AI is removing the middle class of software engineering

    Must read for the AI era.

    You need to contribute beyond what everyone already gets by giving an agent a prompt

    I personally think every engineer will hit a phase like the one mentioned in the blog post due to the usage of AI at work. The blog post reinstates the engineering energy you need to tackle such situation.

  • startups need an asymmetry

    Startups are not easy. All startups are businesses, but not all businesses are startups. This one will help you identify a startup.

  • The human is the loop

    We don’t want the human trapped in the agent loop. The human is the loop, and we tag the agent in occasionally, thoughtfully.

  • Not Holding Back the Ocean

    Must read for engineers trying to navigate the current AI landscape. Discovered this post via a podcast (Next Token, Ep. 3).

  • Write something worth becoming known for

    Wholesome post for aspiring bloggers.

  • Notes from the AI Coding Transition

    I too felt lost in this AI coding transition phase. I am glad that I started reading blogs right now. A blog post like this is exactly what I wanted to read. This post is making me think how I am handling this transition and how can I better handle it.

Books

  • The Inner Game of Tennis

    (read 131 pages)

    Completed reading this book with this batch of papers. This is about a lot of things. It will make you a human being.

  • Tao Te Ching

    (read a few random pages)

    “The way is wide open”

entry.title: Reading Log #2
entry.content:
Here is what I read from 1st to 7th August 2026.

Blogs

  • Never Enough

    A short piece that might bring peace within. My fav lines:

    Maybe we need the misfits who know when to stop. Who leave a conversation unrecorded. Who play with their children without agents running in background. Who can admire another person’s success without feeling diminished by it. Who find peace not by getting ahead, but by no longer needing to

  • Blog about things you don’t understand yet

    Great tips for aspiring bloggers. My learning: you should be learning something while writing a blog post. The signs of learning are that you change your mind a lot as you write, and that your first draft’s conclusion is much better than your introduction - so you end up rewriting the introduction.

    One thing you learn when you try to write poetry is that it is way easier to write to a restrictive structure than it is to simply “write what you feel”

  • The Shape of Things to Come - Part 1

    Harness need to be part of your application, chemically bonded in

    This gave me an instant “we are in a Sci-Fi” moment. It reminded me of this tweet from levelsio: install harness on a VM and do dev there. It is the simplest way to taste the future mentioned in the post. Anyway, I have started experimenting things out for myself.

  • The Shape of Things to Come - Part 2

    The author says that models have actual feelings and that we need to treat agents like real people. In return, they will spend less tokens, make smarter decisions, etc.

    My extreme take after reading both the parts of the blog post: There might be a future, where every project will start with creating a new harness instead of a new git repo.

  • Book Recommendations and Notes

    Nice roundup of books. Took a few and kept them in my future buying list.

  • In defense of not understanding your codebase

    “Theory of the program” is one important concept I learned from the article. I have been thinking of starting a commonplace notebook to jot down the theory of the programs and started one after reading this post. Let us see where it goes.

  • Avoid the trap of magical thinking

    If you are into “how to run engineering teams”, then don’t miss this read.

  • What have note-taking PKMs accomplished, really? and Note-Taking and Personal Knowledge Management

    I am interested in PKMs, so I read them out of curiosity. But I would not recommend these posts for general audience.

  • Don’t be a meat proxy

    Nice articulation of the idea. This is what I meant in the previous reading log as being empathetic towards colleagues. This post is short and to the point.

  • 88 Prompts for Long Term Thinking

    The prompts that I really loved:

    Individually we are better off with expanding possibilities for everyone

    Focus not on the outcomes, but on the processes that produce outcomes

    Every idea about the future is a prediction. Nearly all predictions are wrong. But some are useful

    Our optimism about the future lies not in how small we think our current problems are but how large we believe our capacities for improvement are

    To understand the far future, we must understand the deep past.

  • Pi, Minimal and Performant

    I want to give Pi a try one more time. Maybe third time is the charm?

  • What I Want to Tell You About Orbs

    This is from the folks at amp. I used to use ampcode but they moved on and I think their new thing is orbs. Let me see if I get a chance to explore them sometime.

  • You Should Write An Agent

    The Pi post inspired me to look more closely into the internals of agents, and so I picked this up and read it.

Books

  • Let Go

    (read 21 pages)

    Everyday is not the same. Accept that. Nature is the biggest evidence of this - there is a slight difference in everything that happens everyday. So it is completely okay to not force everyday to look the same, and to make little changes everyday.

  • Norwegian Wood

    (read 10 pages)

    I am trying to get into fiction and started stocking up some books in my shelf. This is one such book. Heard mixed feelings from different people about the book/author. Some like it, and some hate it. I don’t know which band I will be part of.

  • Rework

    (read 5 pages)

  • The Inner Game of Tennis

    (read 30 pages)

    This might be the most important book I’ve read this year so far. My gut says so.
